t: For an additional amount for “Military Construction, Air Force”, for necessary expenses related to the consequences of Hurricane Katrina and other hurricanes of the 2005 season, $97,300,000, to remain available until September 30, 2010: Provided, That such funds may be obligated and expended to carry out planning and design and military construction projects not otherwise authorized by law: Provided further, That the amount provided under this heading is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 402 of H. Con. Res. 95 (109th Congress), the concurrent resolution on the budget for fiscal year 2006.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations provision funding Air Force military construction after the 2005 hurricanes, with an emergency budget designation. The only tempting hook is the reference to a concurrent budget resolution, but that is a budgetary designation inside Congress, not consultation with anyone outside the federal government. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, state or local consultation, rulemaking, or right to sue appears.
fable.s: such funds may be obligated and expended to carry out planning and design and military construction projects not otherwise authorized by law

opus.w: This section only provides an emergency appropriation for Air Force military construction related to the 2005 hurricanes and sets the terms for using the money. The references to planning and design and to the concurrent budget resolution involve only federal actors (the Air Force and Congress). The section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
opus.b: **Step 1, brief analysis.** The tempting reading is that "planning and design" or the reference to a concurrent budget resolution involves some outside process. It doesn't. Planning and design are carried out inside the Air Force. The concurrent resolution is an action of Congress, which is inside the federal government. Nothing here brings in a state, local government, expert, company or member of the public before a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation provision authorizing funds for military construction and planning. It does not require or recommend any form of participation by non-federal entities. The only entities involved are the Air Force (federal agency) and Congress (federal legislature), both of which are inside the federal government. There is no mention of public comment, advisory committees with outside members, or consultation with states or tribes.
qwen_chat.s: For an additional amount for “Military Construction, Air Force”, for necessary expenses related to the consequences of Hurricane Katrina and other hurricanes of the 2005 season, $97,300,000, to remain available until September 30, 2010: Provided, That such funds may be obligated and expended to carry out planning and design and military construction projects not otherwise authorized by law: Provided further, That the amount provided under this heading is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 402 of H. Con. Res. 95 (109th Congress), the concurrent resolution on the budget for fiscal year 2006.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "planning and design" implies consultation with outside parties (e.g., architects, engineers, or local governments). However, the text itself does not mandate such consultation; it merely authorizes the expenditure of funds for these activities. The actors mentioned are the Air Force and the Congress (via the budget resolution), all of which are inside the federal government. There is no mention of public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or coordination with states/tribes.
